title: The Delayed Societal Cost of Unfairness
abstract: arXiv:2611.26030v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Fair machine learning typically evaluates the societal costs of a decision policy -- the loss incurred by the decision-maker (DM) and the unfair distribution of costs among demographic groups of decision-subjects (DS) -- on static data, where reducing one often comes at the expense of the other. Yet decisions change the populations on which they act, and prior work has shown that fairness interventions designed on static data may fail to benefit, or even harm, the disadvantaged group over time. We investigate a complementary question: When can a policy that is Pareto-optimal on pre-deployment data be outperformed by a fairer policy once each is evaluated on the population it induces, reducing costs for one stakeholder without increasing them for the other? translated_title: 不公平的延迟社会代价
translated_abstract: 公平机器学习通常在静态数据上评估决策政策的社会成本——即决策者（DM）所承担的损失，以及在决策对象（DS）不同人口群体之间成本的不公平分布——在这种静态评估框架下，减少一方的成本往往以牺牲另一方为代价。然而，决策会改变其所作用的人群，已有研究表明，基于静态数据设计的公平性干预措施可能无法惠及弱势群体，甚至随时间推移对其造成伤害。我们研究了一个互补的问题：在什么情况下，一个在部署前数据上帕累托最优的政策，一旦在它所诱导出的人群上进行评估，反而会被一个更公平的政策超越——即在不增加另一方成本的情况下降低一方的成本？在资格分数随二元决策及其结果而动态演化的设定中，我们证明，在罗尔斯式公平（即从不降低任何群体的接受率）下……
tldr: 该论文揭示了不公平性的延迟社会代价：在部署前数据上看似帕累托最优的不公平决策政策，在其随时间诱导出的人群上进行评估时，可能被更公平的政策超越，从而在不损害任何一方的情况下同时降低社会成本。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals the delayed societal cost of unfairness, showing that policies appearing Pareto-optimal on pre-deployment data can be outperformed by fairer policies once evaluated on the populations they induce over time.
